proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and define \(p_1(X)=\pi(X)\) and \(p_0(X)=1-\pi(X)\). Since \(Y_a\in[-1,1]\), the conditional mean \(m_a(X):=\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X]\) exists. By consistency, on the event \(\{A=a\}\) one has \(Y=Y_a\), and therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1\{A=a\}Y\mid X]
 =\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1\{A=a\}Y_a\mid X].
\]
Conditional exchangeability gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1\{A=a\}Y_a\mid X]
 =\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X]P(A=a\mid X)
 =m_a(X)p_a(X)
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
On the other hand, the defining conditional-regression property of \(\mu_a\), followed by the tower property, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1\{A=a\}Y\mid X]=p_a(X)\mu_a(X)
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Combining the last three displays yields
\[
 p_a(X)\{\mu_a(X)-m_a(X)\}=0
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The overlap assumption implies \(p_a(X)\ge e_0>0\) almost surely for both \(a=0\) and \(a=1\); division is therefore legitimate and proves
\[
 \mu_a(X)=\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X]
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
By linearity of conditional expectation,
\[
 \mu_1(X)-\mu_0(X)
 =\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X]
 \quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]

It remains to justify pointwise evaluation. By the definition of \(\tau\), it is a representative of \(\mu_1-\mu_0\), and the effect-H\"older assumption makes it continuous on \([0,1]^d\). Suppose that \(f\) and \(g\) are two continuous representatives of the same \(P_X\)-almost-sure equivalence class. If \(f(x)\ne g(x)\) at some \(x\in[0,1]^d\), continuity supplies a nonempty relatively open neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) on which \(|f-g|>0\). Under \(P_X=\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), every such \(U\) has strictly positive \(P_X\)-probability, contradicting \(f=g\) \(P_X\)-almost surely. Thus the continuous representative is unique on all of \([0,1]^d\).

The observed law determines \(\mu_1-\mu_0\) as a \(P_X\)-almost-sure equivalence class by the displayed regression identities, and the uniform-design support property determines its unique continuous representative \(\tau\), hence its value at the fixed interior point \(x_0\). Consequently \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\) is identified, and the notation \(\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x_0]\) denotes this unique continuous representative evaluated at \(x_0\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, overlap, and \(P_X=\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), \(\mu_a(X)\) is a version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X]\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\). The Hölder-continuous representative \(\tau\) of \(\mu_1-\mu_0\) is then the unique continuous representative of \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\), so \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\) is identified, with the pointwise conditional expectation interpreted through this representative.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original claim is too strong because treatment overlap does not imply that \(P_X\) has support at \(x_0\): two continuous functions can agree \(P_X\)-almost surely yet differ at \(x_0\) when the covariate law omits a neighborhood of \(x_0\). The already-frozen uniform-design assumption gives full support and makes the continuous representative unique. This is a narrowing to the model class used by the paper.

proposed.statement: Under consistency, conditional exchangeability, overlap, and \(P_X=\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), \(\mu_a(X)\) is a version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X]\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\). The Hölder-continuous representative \(\tau\) of \(\mu_1-\mu_0\) is then the unique continuous representative of \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\), so \(\theta(P)=\tau_P(x_0)\) is identified, with the pointwise conditional expectation interpreted through this representative.
proposed.justification: The continuous-version convention makes a pointwise causal effect well defined at a covariate value having probability zero.
proposed.gap: Kennedy et al. use the same identifying assumptions; this lemma records the representative needed by the private pointwise problem.
proposed.consumer: It gives the private risk a causal rather than merely regression-functional interpretation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the lemma's dependency and free-symbol metadata with the necessary uniform-design premise in the narrowed claim.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(F_j=N_jB_j\).  Conditional on \(N_j=m\ge2\), the \(m\) records in
\(C_j\) are exchangeable draws from the law conditional on \(X\in C_j\), by
\(\mathrm{ass:iid}\).  The assumed conditional mean of every ordered pair is
\(\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and hence
\[
 \mathbb E_P(B_j\mid N_j=m)=\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}},\qquad
 \mathbb E_PF_j=\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\mathbb E_P[N_j\mathbf 1\{N_j\ge2\}].
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:uniform-design}\) and the definition of \(C_j\),
\(N_j\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,v)\).  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E[N_j\mathbf 1\{N_j\ge2\}]
 =\mathbb EN_j-\Pr(N_j=1)
 =nv-nv(1-v)^{n-1}.
\]
Summing this identity over the \(k\) cells proves the displayed expectation.

It remains to check replacement sensitivity.  For a cell containing \(m\)
records, write
\[
 F_m=\frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i\ne r}Z_{\mathrm{pair}}(O_i,O_r),\qquad m\ge2,
\]
and set \(F_0=F_1=0\).  Remove one record.  If \(m=2\), then
\(|F_2-F_1|\le2\).  If \(m\ge3\), decompose the ordered-pair sum as
\(U'+V\), where \(U'\) contains pairs of surviving records and \(V\)
contains the pairs involving the removed record.  Symmetry and
\(|Z_{\mathrm{pair}}|\le1\) give
\(|U'|\le(m-1)(m-2)\) and \(|V|\le2(m-1)\).  Consequently
\[
 \left|\frac{U'+V}{m-1}-\frac{U'}{m-2}\right|
 \le \frac{|V|}{m-1}+\frac{|U'|}{(m-1)(m-2)}\le3.
\]
Addition has the same bound by reversal.  Replacing a record is a removal
followed by an addition, possibly in a different cell, so
\[
 |S_{\mathrm{occ}}(D_n)-S_{\mathrm{occ}}(D_n')|\le6\le12.
\]
Finally, for \(x=(n-1)v\), Bernoulli's inequality and
\((1-v)^{n-1}\le e^{-x}\) imply
\[
 (1-e^{-1})\min\{1,x\}
 \le1-(1-v)^{n-1}\le\min\{1,x\}.
\]
Because \(n\ge2\), \(x\) and \(nv\) differ by at most a factor two.
Substitution into the exact expectation, followed by \(kv\asymp h^d\) and
\(v\asymp\ell^d\), proves the last assertion.  Division by twelve is valid
because the preceding deterministic sensitivity bound is finite and positive.

For a fixed dataset write
\(w_t(D_n)=\exp\{-\epsilon Q_t(D_n)/2\}\) and
\(Z(D_n)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal G_r}w_u(D_n)\).  If \(D_n\sim_1D_n'\), the
sensitivity hypothesis gives
\[
 e^{-\epsilon/2}w_t(D_n')\le w_t(D_n)\le e^{\epsilon/2}w_t(D_n'),
 \qquad
 e^{-\epsilon/2}Z(D_n')\le Z(D_n)\le e^{\epsilon/2}Z(D_n').
\]
Thus, for every \(t\),
\[
 \frac{\Pr(T_{\mathrm{shell}}=t\mid D_n)}
 {\Pr(T_{\mathrm{shell}}=t\mid D_n')}
 =\frac{w_t(D_n)}{w_t(D_n')}\frac{Z(D_n')}{Z(D_n)}\le e^\epsilon.
\]
Summation over an arbitrary subset of \(\mathcal G_r\) proves pure
\(\epsilon\)-differential privacy under \(\sim_1\).

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_H\).  The denominator of the selector contains the
term indexed by \(t_P\), so pointwise in \(D_n\),
\[
 \Pr(T_{\mathrm{shell}}=t\mid D_n)
 \le 1\wedge\exp\{-\epsilon(Q_t(D_n)-Q_{t_P}(D_n))/2\}.
\]
The grid definition gives \(|t_P-\theta(P)|\le r\).  The grid points with
\(|t-t_P|<r\) contribute less than \(r\) to the conditional expectation of
\(|T_{\mathrm{shell}}-t_P|\).  Every remaining point lies in exactly one
\(\mathcal S_m(P;r)\), \(m\ge1\), and then
\(|t-t_P|<(m+1)r\).  Taking expectation under \(P^{\otimes n}\) and using
the preceding pointwise probability bound yields
\[
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}|T_{\mathrm{shell}}-t_P|
 \le r+r\sum_{m\ge1}(m+1)\sum_{t\in\mathcal S_m(P;r)}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[1\wedge
 e^{-\epsilon(Q_t-Q_{t_P})/2}\right]
 \le (B_{\mathrm{shell}}+1)r.
\]
The triangle inequality and \(|t_P-\theta(P)|\le r\) now give the sharper
bound \((B_{\mathrm{shell}}+2)r\), and hence the asserted
\((B_{\mathrm{shell}}+3)r\).  No step sums an unweighted unit bound over
\(\mathcal G_r\), which proves the stated absence of a grid-cardinality or
nuisance-sieve factor.

We prove the three lower bounds separately.  Constants denoted by \(c,C\)
below depend only on \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), and may change from
line to line.

First, privacy cannot improve nonprivate risk.  Given any private Markov
kernel \(T\), define its conditional barycenter
\(\bar T(D_n)=\int t\,T(dt\mid D_n)\).  Since the output is in \([-2,2]\),
\(\bar T\) is a measurable nonprivate estimator with the same range.  By
conditional Jensen,
\[
 |\bar T(D_n)-\theta(P)|
 \le\int|t-\theta(P)|\,T(dt\mid D_n).
\]
Taking expectations, then the supremum over \(P\in\mathcal M_H\), and
finally the infimum over private \(T\), gives
\(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\).

For the dense branch, choose a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) bump \(g\), supported
on the unit cube and equal to one at the origin.  For a separation
\(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), put
\(h=c_0\delta^{1/\gamma}\) and
\(g_h(x)=g((x-x_0)/h)\), with \(c_0,\delta_0\) small enough that the support
lies in \([0,1]^d\) by the interior condition on \(x_0\).  Consider two laws
with uniform \(X\), independent \(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\),
\(\mu_0=0\), and \(\tau_0=0\), \(\tau_1=\delta g_h\).  Conditional on
\((X,A)\), take \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) with mean \(\mu_A\), and construct
potential outcomes with these means independently of \(A\) given \(X\),
then impose consistency.  Scaling of the bump gives
\(\|\tau_1\|_{\mathcal H^\gamma}\le L\); all other Hölder conditions and
overlap hold, so both laws lie in \(\mathcal M_H\).  Their target separation
is \(\delta\).  A direct calculation on the two atoms of \(Y\) gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_0,P_1)
 \le C\delta\int\mathbf 1\{g_h(x)\ne0\}\,dx
 \le C\delta h^d.
\]
Couple \(X\) and \(A\) identically and draw the two binary outcomes from a
common uniform random variable; their conditional mismatch probability is
the absolute difference of their Bernoulli success probabilities.
Coordinatewise repetition therefore couples the product laws with expected
Hamming distance \(D\le Cn\delta h^d\).  Apply
\(\mathrm{lem:private-le-cam-coupling}\) with privacy slack zero.  For
\(\delta=c_1(n\epsilon)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)}=c_1\rho_G\), choose \(c_1\) so
that \(10\epsilon D\le1\).  Thresholding any estimator at the midpoint of
the two target values turns it into a test, and on a testing error its
absolute estimation loss is at least \(\delta/2\).  The cited testing bound
therefore gives risk at least \(c\delta\).  If this choice exceeds
\(\delta_0\), use the fixed separation \(\delta_0\); since \(\rho_G\le1\),
decreasing the final constant gives the bound for all \(n\epsilon\ge1\).

We next construct the sparse two-fiber experiment.  The details are included
because exact one-record cancellation is essential for the claimed exponent.
Let \(G_h=g_h^2\).  Start with a fixed nonnegative smooth function
\(\eta\), positive on \([-1/2,1/2]^d\) and supported on \([-1,1]^d\).
For the lattice of mesh \(\ell\), normalize its translates by
\[
 w_j(x)=\frac{\eta((x-z_j)/\ell)}
 {\{\sum_m\eta((x-z_m)/\ell)^2\}^{1/2}}.
\]
The denominator is bounded away from zero, only a dimension-dependent
number of terms overlap, and \(\sum_jw_j^2=1\).  Thus
\(\phi_j=g_hw_j\) satisfies
\[
 \sum_j\phi_j(x)^2=G_h(x),\qquad
 \|\phi_j\|_{\mathcal H^s}\le C\ell^{-s}\quad(s>0),
\]
and only \(k\asymp h^d/\ell^d\) functions meet the support of \(g_h\).
For independent Rademacher signs \(\lambda_j\), put
\(f_\lambda=\sum_j\lambda_j\phi_j\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb E_\lambda f_\lambda(x)=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_\lambda f_\lambda(x)^2=G_h(x).
\]
Take \(a=c_2\ell^\alpha\), \(b=c_2\ell^\beta\), and
\(\delta=4ab\), and choose \(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\).  Because
\(q=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), one has
\(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\le h\) after decreasing \(c_2,\delta_0\).

It is convenient here to take \(Y\in\{0,1\}\), still a subset of its
declared support.  If \(\alpha\ge\beta\), define the first fiber by
\[
 \pi_{P,\lambda}=\tfrac12,\quad
 \mu_{0,P,\lambda}=\tfrac12+b f_\lambda-\tfrac12\delta G_h,
 \quad \tau_{P,\lambda}=\delta G_h,
\]
and the second by
\[
 \pi_{Q,\lambda}=\tfrac12+a f_\lambda,\quad
 \mu_{0,Q,\lambda}=\tfrac12+b f_\lambda,
 \quad \tau_{Q,\lambda}=0.
\]
If \(\beta>\alpha\), instead use
\[
 \pi_{P,\lambda}=\pi_{Q,\lambda}=\tfrac12+a f_\lambda,\quad
 \mu_{0,P,\lambda}=\tfrac12-\tfrac12\delta G_h,\quad
 \tau_{P,\lambda}=\delta G_h,
\]
and
\[
 \mu_{0,Q,\lambda}=\tfrac12+b f_\lambda,\qquad
 \tau_{Q,\lambda}=0.
\]
The scaling bounds above show respectively that the propensity, control
regression, and effect have Hölder norms bounded by \(L\).  Smallness of
\(c_2\) places every propensity and conditional mean in \([1/4,3/4]\), so
the overlap condition follows from \(e_0\le1/4\).  As in the dense
construction, conditionally independent potential outcomes give
exchangeability and consistency.  Hence every component law belongs to
\(\mathcal M_H\).  Every first-fiber law has target \(\delta\), whereas every
second-fiber law has target zero.

We verify the cancellation.  Write \(s=2A-1\) and \(z=2Y-1\).  In the case
\(\alpha\ge\beta\), the four conditional masses, multiplied by four, are
\[
 p_\lambda=1+2zb f_\lambda+sz\delta G_h,\qquad
 q_\lambda=1+2sa f_\lambda+2zb f_\lambda+4szab f_\lambda^2.
\]
In the case \(\beta>\alpha\), they are
\[
 p_\lambda=1+2sa f_\lambda+sz\delta G_h+2za\delta f_\lambda G_h,
 \qquad
 q_\lambda=1+2sa f_\lambda+2zb f_\lambda+4szab f_\lambda^2.
\]
The two displayed moment identities and \(\delta=4ab\) show in either case
that \(\mathbb E_\lambda p_\lambda=\mathbb E_\lambda q_\lambda\) for every
\((x,s,z)\).  Thus the one-record prior predictives agree exactly.

For completeness, we bound the cost when signs are reused.  Conditional on
the covariates, join indices whose active \(\phi_j\)'s share a sign.  The
overlap degree of the underlying lattice is bounded in terms of \(d\), and
different connected components use independent signs.  For a component of
size \(m\), expand the products of the preceding four-atom masses and average
each sign.  Constant and one-record terms cancel by the preceding identity.
Every remaining term that differs between the fibers contains either one
factor \(\delta\), a product \(ab=\delta/4\), or two copies of the nuisance
amplitude absent from one fiber.  That absent amplitude is \(a\) when
\(\alpha\ge\beta\), and \(b\) when \(\beta>\alpha\); respectively
\(a^2\le ab\) and \(b^2\le ab\).  Summing the product expansion therefore
gives the explicit component bound
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\overline P_m,\overline Q_m)
 \le C\delta (m)_2(1+c_2)^m. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, choose the first two record positions carrying one of the listed
factors in at most \((m)_2\) ways; the absolute sum over every remaining
position is bounded by the binomial expansion \((1+c_2)^m\).  Averaging
Rademacher monomials and summing the four atoms cannot increase this absolute
bound.  This proves (1), rather than assuming a collision property as part of
the construction.

For each component, put the pointwise minimum of its two finite probability
masses on the diagonal and couple the residual masses arbitrarily.  The
failure probability is exactly the component total variation in (1); on
failure replace all of its records, so the Hamming cost is at most \(m\).
If \(M_i\) is one plus the
number of other covariates within a fixed multiple of \(\ell\) of \(X_i\),
(1) and bounded overlap imply
\[
 \mathbb E[d_{\mathrm{Ham}}\mid X_1,\ldots,X_n]
 \le C\delta\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\operatorname{supp}(g_h)\}
 \mathbf 1\{M_i\ge2\}M_i^2(1+c_2)^{M_i}.
\]
Under the uniform design, conditional on \(X_i\), \(M_i-1\) is dominated
by \(\operatorname{Bin}(n-1,C\ell^d)\).  When \(n\ell^d\le1\), its
exponentially weighted moments are bounded and
\[
 \mathbb E[\mathbf 1\{M_i\ge2\}M_i^2(1+c_2)^{M_i}\mid X_i]
 \le Cn\ell^d.
\]
Also \(\Pr\{X_i\in\operatorname{supp}(g_h)\}\le Ch^d\).  We have therefore
constructed a coupling of the two prior-predictive samples with
\[
 D\le C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d
 =C n^2\delta^{,1+d/\gamma+d/q}. \tag{2}
\]

Now suppose \(\rho_F\ge\rho_G\).  The uncapped radii apply because
\(n\epsilon\ge1\), and
\[
 \rho_F^{D_F}=(n^2\epsilon)^{-1},\qquad
 \rho_G^{1+d/\gamma}=(n\epsilon)^{-1}.
\]
If \(n\rho_F^{d/q}>1\), then
\[
 \rho_F^{1+d/\gamma}
 =\frac{\rho_F^{D_F}}{\rho_F^{d/q}}
 <\frac{1}{n\epsilon}=\rho_G^{1+d/\gamma},
\]
contradicting \(\rho_F\ge\rho_G\).  Hence the sparse condition required in
(2) holds after the harmless fixed rescaling used to define \(\ell\).  Set
\(\delta=c_3\rho_F\).  Equation (2) gives
\[
 \epsilon D\le C\epsilon n^2\delta^{D_F}=Cc_3^{D_F}.
\]
Choose \(c_3\) so this is at most a fixed small constant and apply
\(\mathrm{lem:private-le-cam-coupling}\) to the two convex hulls.  Midpoint
thresholding again converts estimation to testing and gives risk at least
\(c\delta=c\rho_F\).  If \(\rho_F<\rho_G\), the already proved
\(c\rho_G\) lower bound implies the \(\rho_F\) bound.  Fixed-separation
versions handle the finitely many scale choices above \(\delta_0\), exactly
as in the dense branch.

We have shown lower bounds by fixed positive multiples of each of
\(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_G,\rho_F\).  Taking the smallest of the three
constants proves their maximum lower bound and the theorem.

Assume the affirmative premise in the statement.  At
\(r=C_{\mathrm{scale}}\rho_\star\), it supplies a finite score family with
replacement sensitivity at most one and
\(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le C_{\mathrm{shell}}\).  Applying
\(\mathrm{prop:shell-risk}\) gives an explicitly data-dependent pure
\(\epsilon\)-private selector satisfying
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
 |T_{\mathrm{shell}}-\theta(P)|
 \le (C_{\mathrm{shell}}+3)C_{\mathrm{scale}}\rho_\star.
\]
Thus one may take
\(C_{\mathrm{upper}}=(C_{\mathrm{shell}}+3)C_{\mathrm{scale}}\), and the
definition of the private minimax risk gives
\(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\le C_{\mathrm{upper}}\rho_\star\).  The
opposite inequality is \(\mathrm{thm:full-class-lower-frontier}\).  By the
definition of \(\rho_\star\), these two inequalities are exactly
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
 \asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F.
\]
The upper proof uses only the ordered shell sum, whose assumed bound is
independent of the nuisance-sieve dimension; consequently it introduces no
nuisance-sieve logarithm.  The formula contains the nonprivate minimax risk
as one branch and the two additional pure-privacy radii as the other
branches, which is the asserted extension.

By \(\mathrm{lem:nonprivate-cate-rate-floor}\),
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\ge c\left\{
 n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\vee n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/q)}\right\}. \tag{1}
\]
Fix \(\epsilon\in(0,1]\), independently of \(n\).  The definitions give
\[
 \rho_G\le C_\epsilon n^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)},\qquad
 \rho_F\le C_\epsilon n^{-2/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)}.
\]
Since
\[
 \frac{1}{1+d/\gamma}>\frac{1}{2+d/\gamma},\qquad
 \frac{2}{1+d/\gamma+d/q}>\frac{2}{2+d/\gamma+d/q},
\]
each privacy radius is bounded by a constant multiple of the corresponding
term on the right of (1).  Hence
\(\rho_G\vee\rho_F=O(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}})\).  Substitution in
\(\mathrm{thm:combined-private-frontier}\) gives
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}.
\]
The condition \(q<\gamma\) ensures throughout that the common model is the
declared two-scale class; the exponent comparisons themselves require only
positivity of \(q\) and \(\gamma\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(p_1\in\operatorname{co}(\mathcal P_1)\) and
\(p_2\in\operatorname{co}(\mathcal P_2)\), and suppose a coupling
\((U,V)\) of \(p_1,p_2\) satisfies
\(D=\mathbb E[d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(U,V)]\).  Every
\((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-differentially private test has error
\[
 P_e\ge\frac12\max\{1-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p_1,p_2),
 0.9e^{-10\varepsilon D}-10D\delta\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Let \(p_1\in\operatorname{co}(\mathcal P_1)\) and \(p_2\in\operatorname{co}(\mathcal P_2)\). Let \((X,Y)\) be a coupling between \(p_1\) and \(p_2\) with \(D=\mathbb E[d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(X,Y)]\). Then for \(\varepsilon\ge0\) and \(\delta\ge0\), any \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-differentially private hypothesis testing algorithm \(\widehat\theta\) must satisfy \(P_e(\widehat\theta,\mathcal P_1,\mathcal P_2)\ge\frac12\max\{1-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(p_1,p_2),0.9e^{-10\varepsilon D}-10D\delta\}\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021), Theorem 1, equation (4), in the PMLR published version.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), let
\(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\) and
\(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\).  There is a sufficiently small constant
\(c_0>0\), depending only on \(d\), such that, if \(n\ell^d\le c_0\),
there are two priors on
laws in \(\mathcal M_H\), one supported on \(\theta(P)=\delta\) and the
other on \(\theta(P)=0\), such that their one-record prior predictives are
identical, their \(n\)-record prior predictives admit a coupling with
\[
 \mathbb E d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(D_n,D_n')
 \le C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d,
\]
and their squared Hellinger distance is at most
\(C n^2\delta^2h^d\ell^d\).  The constants depend only on
\(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We give the construction explicitly.  Let \(g_h\) be a smooth bump supported
in a side-\(h\) cube about \(x_0\), with \(g_h(x_0)=1\), and put
\(G_h=g_h^2\).  If \(\eta\) is a fixed smooth bump whose lattice translates
cover \(\mathbb R^d\), define the quadratic partition
\[
 w_j(x)=\frac{\eta((x-z_j)/\ell)}
 {\{\sum_m\eta((x-z_m)/\ell)^2\}^{1/2}},\qquad
 \phi_j=g_hw_j.
\]
The denominator is uniformly positive, overlap is bounded, and hence
\(\sum_j\phi_j^2=G_h\) and
\(\|\phi_j\|_{\mathcal H^s}\le C\ell^{-s}\).  For independent Rademacher
signs \(\lambda_j\), let \(f_\lambda=\sum_j\lambda_j\phi_j\).  Then
\(\mathbb E_\lambda f_\lambda=0\) and
\(\mathbb E_\lambda f_\lambda^2=G_h\).

Choose \(a=c\ell^\alpha\), \(b=c\ell^\beta\), and \(\delta=4ab\), adjusting
fixed scale constants so that \(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\).  When
\(\alpha\ge\beta\), use
\[
 (\pi_P,\mu_{0,P},\tau_P)
 =(1/2,1/2+bf_\lambda-\delta G_h/2,\delta G_h),
 \quad
 (\pi_Q,\mu_{0,Q},\tau_Q)
 =(1/2+af_\lambda,1/2+bf_\lambda,0).
\]
When \(\beta>\alpha\), use
\[
 (\pi_P,\mu_{0,P},\tau_P)
 =(1/2+af_\lambda,1/2-\delta G_h/2,\delta G_h),
 \quad
 (\pi_Q,\mu_{0,Q},\tau_Q)
 =(1/2+af_\lambda,1/2+bf_\lambda,0).
\]
Let \(X\) be uniform, let \(Y\in\{0,1\}\) conditionally have the displayed
regression, and construct potential outcomes conditionally independently of
\(A\) before imposing consistency.  Scaled smoothness, \(q<\gamma\), and a
sufficiently small fixed \(c\) put all these laws in \(\mathcal M_H\) and
keep propensities and regressions in \([1/4,3/4]\).

With \(s=2A-1\) and \(z=2Y-1\), four times the conditional masses in the
first case are
\[
 p_\lambda=1+2zbf_\lambda+sz\delta G_h,\qquad
 q_\lambda=1+2saf_\lambda+2zbf_\lambda+4szabf_\lambda^2,
\]
and in the second case they are
\[
 p_\lambda=1+2saf_\lambda+sz\delta G_h+2za\delta f_\lambda G_h,
 \qquad
 q_\lambda=1+2saf_\lambda+2zbf_\lambda+4szabf_\lambda^2.
\]
The two Rademacher moment identities and \(4ab=\delta\) prove equality of
the one-record mixtures.

Condition on all covariates and join two record indices when their active
\(\phi_j\)'s overlap.  Different graph components use independent signs.
For a component of size \(m\), expand its product masses and average the
signs.  The degree-zero and degree-one terms cancel.  Every remaining
difference contains \(\delta\), \(ab=\delta/4\), or two copies of the
nuisance amplitude absent from one fiber.  That last amplitude is \(a\) if
\(\alpha\ge\beta\) and \(b\) otherwise, and respectively
\(a^2\le ab\) or \(b^2\le ab\).  Choosing the first two involved record
positions and summing all residual factors by the binomial theorem gives
\[
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\overline P_m,\overline Q_m)
 \le C\delta(m)_2(1+c)^m. \tag{4}
\]
For each finite component law, put the pointwise minimum of the two masses
on the diagonal and couple the residual masses arbitrarily.  Its failure
probability is the total variation in (4); replace all \(m\) records on a
failure.  A collision neighborhood count is dominated by
\(1+\operatorname{Bin}(n-1,C\ell^d)\); its required exponentially weighted
moments are bounded when \(n\ell^d\le c_0\); smallness of \(c_0\) makes the
bounded-degree component exploration subcritical.  There are at most \(Cnh^d\)
records in the macro support in expectation, and each has collision
probability at most \(Cn\ell^d\).  Equation (4) therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb E d_{\mathrm{Ham}}(D_n,D_n')
 \le C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d.
\]
For Hellinger distance, square the component likelihood difference before
summing.  Equality of the one-record mixtures again makes a collision
necessary, while (4)'s first nonzero coefficient has magnitude at most
\(C\delta\).  The same collision count and exponential-moment calculation
gives
\[
 H^2\!\left(\int P_\lambda^{\otimes n}d\varpi,
              \int Q_\lambda^{\otimes n}d\varpi\right)
 \le Cn^2\delta^2h^d\ell^d.
\]
This proves every claimed property from the displayed construction.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is a constant \(c>0\), depending only on
\(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), such that
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\ge c\left\{
 n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\vee
 n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/q)}\right\}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For the first term, take uniform \(X\), independent
\(A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), \(\mu_0=0\), and compare
\(\tau=0\) with \(\tau=\delta g((\cdot-x_0)/h)\), where
\(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\) and the smooth bump is supported inside the
cube.  Conditional binary outcomes and conditionally independent potential
outcomes put both laws in \(\mathcal M_H\).  Their squared Hellinger distance
for one observation is at most \(C\delta^2h^d\).  Tensorization gives
\[
 H^2(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n})\le Cn\delta^{2+d/\gamma}.
\]
Taking \(\delta=c n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)}\), with \(c\) small, makes total
variation bounded away from one because
\(d_{\mathrm{TV}}\le H\).  The latter inequality follows directly from
Cauchy--Schwarz:
\[
 \frac12\int|p-q|
 =\frac12\int|\sqrt p-\sqrt q|(\sqrt p+\sqrt q)
 \le H(P,Q),
\]
under the convention \(H^2=\int(\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\).  For every test
\(\varphi\), directly from the
definition of total variation,
\[
 P_0(\varphi=1)+P_1(\varphi=0)
 =1-\{P_1(\varphi=1)-P_0(\varphi=1)\}
 \ge1-d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_0^{\otimes n},P_1^{\otimes n}).
\]
Thresholding an estimator at the midpoint incurs loss at least
\(\delta/2\) on a testing error.  Averaging the two risks therefore gives
the first lower bound.

For the second, apply \(\mathrm{lem:two-fiber-distance-certificate}\).  Its
exact equality of one-record prior predictives and its Hellinger conclusion
give
\[
 H^2\!\left(\int P_\lambda^{\otimes n}d\varpi(\lambda),
              \int Q_\lambda^{\otimes n}d\varpi(\lambda)\right)
 \le Cn^2\delta^2h^d\ell^d
 =Cn^2\delta^{,2+d/\gamma+d/q}, \tag{3}
\]
whenever \(n\ell^d\le C\).

Set \(\delta=c n^{-2/(2+d/\gamma+d/q)}\).  If
\(d/q>2+d/\gamma\), then \(n\ell^d\le C\), and (3), followed by the same
displayed total-variation testing identity, proves the second lower bound.  If
\(d/q\le2+d/\gamma\), then
\[
 \frac{2}{2+d/\gamma+d/q}\ge\frac{1}{2+d/\gamma},
\]
so the second displayed rate is no larger than the first and is already
covered by the deterministic bump lower bound.  This proves the maximum in
all regimes.  Fixed-separation bumps allow the constant to be reduced so the
claim also covers bounded \(n\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose \(n\ge 2\), \(Z_{\mathrm{pair}}\in[-1,1]\) is symmetric, and
\(\mathbb E_P[Z_{\mathrm{pair}}(O_1,O_2)\mid X_1,X_2\in C_j]=\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\)
for every \(j\). Then
\[
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}S_{\mathrm{occ}}
 =\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}knv\{1-(1-v)^{n-1}\}.
\]
Moreover,
\(\sup_{D_n\sim_1D_n'}|S_{\mathrm{occ}}(D_n)-S_{\mathrm{occ}}(D_n')|\le 12\).
Under the public partition comparabilities \(kv\asymp h^d\) and
\(v\asymp\ell^d\), the magnitude of the sensitivity-normalized private
signal is therefore
\[
 \frac{\epsilon}{12}\left|\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}S_{\mathrm{occ}}\right|
 \asymp \epsilon|\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}}|nh^d\min\{1,n\ell^d\},
\]
with constants independent of whether \(n\ell^d\) is smaller or larger than one.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The exact binomial factor is zero at \(n=1\), whereas \(\min\{1,n\ell^d\}\) is positive. The order consequence therefore needs \(n\) at least two and must explicitly use the public partition comparabilities; the identity and sensitivity bound themselves remain valid.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
There is a constant \(c_{\mathrm{lower}}>0\), depending only on
\(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,e_0\), such that throughout \(n\epsilon\ge1\),
\[
 R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
 \ge c_{\mathrm{lower}}\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee\rho_G\vee\rho_F\}.
\]
The \(\rho_G\) term is witnessed by a localized one-record subexperiment.
For the \(\rho_F\) term, whenever \(\rho_F\ge\rho_G\), there are smooth
shared-sign two-fiber mixtures in \(\mathcal M_H\), separated by
\(\delta\asymp\rho_F\), whose prior-predictive samples admit a coupling with
expected Hamming distance at most
\(C\delta n^2h^d\ell^d\), where
\(h\asymp\delta^{1/\gamma}\),
\(\ell\asymp\delta^{1/q}\), and \(n\ell^d\le C\).  If
\(\rho_F<\rho_G\), the \(\rho_F\) lower bound is already implied by the
\(\rho_G\) branch.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original explanatory sentence asserts an unscaled dense-regime Hamming transport order. The private Le Cam calculation uses an amplitude-weighted sparse coupling only when \(\rho_F\) is not dominated by \(\rho_G\); in the complementary regime the dense one-record branch already supplies the lower bound. The replacement preserves the headline inequality and states exactly the coupling proved.

proposed.justification: A same-class converse determines whether dense occupancy creates a new privacy radius or merely activates the first-order branch.
proposed.gap: Kennedy et al. give only the nonprivate term, and Acharya et al. give generic coupling inequalities rather than the occupancy-indexed causal mixtures needed for the two privacy terms.
proposed.consumer: It prevents an upper mechanism from being certified against a surrogate regression class or only a sparse diagnostic family.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Add the cited private Le Cam theorem to the declared proof spine and synchronize the node with the proposed narrowed explanatory sentence.

proposed.statement: For fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,1]\) and \(q<\gamma\), both \(\rho_G\) and \(\rho_F\) are no larger in order than \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\). Hence Theorem 2 reduces to \(R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), the Kennedy et al. pointwise-CATE frontier, whenever privacy does not shrink with \(n\).
proposed.justification: The required special-case reduction checks that privacy does not spuriously degrade the classical fixed-budget asymptotics.
proposed.gap: This reduction is a consistency check against Kennedy et al., not a separate novelty claim.
proposed.consumer: It lets applied users recover the established nonprivate benchmark in regimes where privacy is asymptotically free.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the proved nonprivate rate floor used in the exponent comparison.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct explicit target-indexed scores \(Q_t\) on the entire composite class \(\mathcal M_H\) and prove the uniform weighted-shell bound \(\mathfrak W_r(Q)\le C_{\mathrm{shell}}\) at \(r=C_{\mathrm{scale}}\rho_\star\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen handle specifies procedural verbs but no score formula, nuisance sieve, clipping envelope, or composite-test separation inequality. The occupancy lemma controls the mean and sensitivity of one fixed pair kernel; it does not show that profiled full-fiber kernels retain a common signed separation, and the shell proposition assumes rather than proves the required weighted tail sum.
open_obligations.attempted: Occupancy-weighted fixed-kernel scores close on a shared-sign two-fiber subfamily, but profiling finite nuisance sieves introduces an uncovered entropy factor. Replacing the scores by direct local treated/control averages gives a valid full-class private estimator, but only at the slower regression rate recorded below and therefore does not certify the requested rho-star shell family.
open_obligations.partial_result:
An unconditional loose upper bound is nevertheless obtainable on the same
class.  For a cube \(B_H\) of side \(H\) about \(x_0\), form
\(N_a=\sum_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_H,A_i=a\}\) and
\(S_a=\sum_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_H,A_i=a\}Y_i\).  Release the four-vector
\((N_0,N_1,S_0,S_1)\) with independent Laplace noise of scale
\(8/\epsilon\), and set
\[
 \widehat\mu_a=
 \Pi_{[-1,1]}\!\left(
 \frac{\widetilde S_a}{\max\{\widetilde N_a,e_0nH^d/2\}}
 \right),\qquad
 \widehat\theta_H=\Pi_{[-2,2]}(\widehat\mu_1-\widehat\mu_0).
\]
The vector has replacement \(\ell_1\)-sensitivity at most four, so this
release is pure \(\epsilon\)-private.  Uniform design and overlap give
\(\mathbb EN_a\ge e_0nH^d\).  Since
\(\mu_1=\mu_0+\tau\) and \(q<\gamma\) imply that both regressions are
\(\beta\)-Hölder, bounded-variable concentration and the first absolute
moment of Laplace noise give
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_H-\theta(P)|
 \le C\left\{H^\beta+(nH^d)^{-1/2}+(n\epsilon H^d)^{-1}\right\}.
\]
Taking
\(H\asymp n^{-1/(2\beta+d)}\vee(n\epsilon)^{-1/(\beta+d)}\), truncated at
\(1/4\), proves the honest bracket
\[
 c\rho_\star\le R_{n,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{DP}}
 \le C\left[1\wedge\left\{
 n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}\vee
 (n\epsilon)^{-\beta/(\beta+d)}\right\}\right].
\]
This does not prove the requested \(\rho_\star\)-scale score family: it is a
first-order regression fallback and can be strictly slower than the desired
two-fiber rate.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine the smallest simultaneous adaptation factor over the compact smoothness range \(\Theta_{\mathrm{sm}}\) for one pure-private scalar release.
open_obligations.obstruction: The base rho-star score family remains unconstructed, and the adaptive handle does not define the joint score array or its global replacement sensitivity. Without that geometry, neither a correlated-noise upper bound nor an adaptive testing lower bound has a well-typed object to analyze.
open_obligations.attempted: A finite multiscale release under basic composition was compared with the desired one-shot release. It yields the explicit benchmark below after replacing epsilon by epsilon divided by the number of scales, but it cannot identify whether this factor is necessary or can be reduced by correlation and post-processing.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved fixed-class ingredients show that any successful adaptive release
must control, on the same privacy transcript, both a dense scale satisfying
\(n\epsilon r^{1+d/\gamma}\asymp1\) and a sparse scale satisfying
\(n^2\epsilon r^{1+d/\gamma+d/q}\asymp1\).  Releasing \(J\) candidate
arrays separately by basic composition replaces \(\epsilon\) by
\(\epsilon/J\), which gives the explicit but generally nonoptimal benchmark
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\vee
 (n\epsilon/J)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)}\vee
 (n^2\epsilon/J)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)}.
\]
No conclusion about the smallest possible logarithmic factor follows until
the joint sensitivity or correlated-noise geometry of the one-shot array is
specified.
